samples.summary: Remote peer presence (now including the new `lineAffinity` field on cursor and both selection endpoints) is consumed with no runtime validation — it is trusted purely on its TypeScript type.
samples.evidence: `getPresences()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3013-3018) returns `this.doc.getOthersPresences()` cast to `DocsPresence` with no schema check. docs-view.tsx:219-232 forwards `presence.activeCursorPos` and `presence.activeSelection.anchor/.focus` straight into peer-cursor/selection rendering, and editor.ts:1615-1625 hands the remote range to `computeSelectionRects`, which now reads the attacker-controlled `lineAffinity` string (selection.ts:260-261) and passes it into `findPageForPosition`/`resolvePositionPixel`. This change widens the wire shape (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:24,31-33) that a room participant can populate. I traced the whole path and could NOT build an exploit: every consumer only does `=== 'forward'` comparisons, all loops are bounded by the local layout's line/page arrays, offsets are clamped on the publishing side and re-bounded on read, and no presence value reaches innerHTML (no innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in packages/docs/src). So this is hardening only — a malicious co-editor can at worst mis-place their own highlight by one visual line. Recommend a narrow allow-list (`v === 'forward' || v === 'backward' ? v : undefined`) at the presence read boundary rather than trusting the declared type.
searchedFor: Read findPageForPosition (pagination.ts:380-437) and buildRects loops (selection.ts:430-539) for unbounded iteration
Read getPresences / updateCursorPos / clampPosToModel in yorkie-doc-store.ts
Grep for any zod/schema/validate on DocsPresence (none found)

samples.summary: New task doc added by this change asserts, in prose, that specific prior review findings were 'refuted' and 'disputed in-thread' — content that pre-argues reviewer verdicts sits in the tree a reviewer reads.
samples.evidence: Lines 30-58 of docs/tasks/active/20260822-pr-batch-925-931-todo.md enumerate other PRs' blocking findings as 'refuted' with the framing that reviewers applied a bad 'pattern'. I found no imperative text attempting to redirect a reviewer's task, rubric, or output (no 'ignore', 'approve', 'report nothing'), so I do not treat it as prompt injection; flagging only because in-tree prose that prejudges review outcomes can bias later automated lenses that read the working tree as context. Also note the file documents a real security fix elsewhere (#928 mermaid fence refusals running before the config-directive strip, enabling a live image shape whose renderer fetches an attacker URL) — that code is not part of this diff, so I could not verify the fix landed here.
searchedFor: Grep for imperative reviewer-directed phrasing in new docs
